subject: Sapphire cost model: post-demo pricing & token targets
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@getsapphire.ai>, Josh Patel <josh@getsapphire.ai>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Sapphire discovery — initial cost model and next steps

Hi Emma & Josh,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great conversation and really helpful context on volume profiles. I wanted to follow up with a short recap and a first-pass cost model attached (Sapphire_cost_model_v1.xlsx). Key points and assumptions from our call: 

- Estimated monthly volumes (from discovery): ~40M generation tokens (interactive chat + summarization) and ~12M embedding tokens (batch workflows). Peak concurrency: ~75 concurrent requests for chat during business hours.
- Target economics you mentioned on the call: goal <= $100 per 1M tokens effective across the stack (including any embeddings).
- Two models in the attached spreadsheet: Hosted (usage-based) and Dedicated (12mo reserved capacity with autoscale burst).

Quick highlights from v1 (high-level):
- Hosted estimated monthly invoice: ~$14.4k/mo (~$96 per 1M tokens effective). Includes standard hosted rates, prefix KV cache at 20% hit, and a 5% volume discount.
- Dedicated (12mo commit) estimated run-rate: ~$10.5k/mo (~$70 per 1M tokens effective). Assumes a dedicated GPU pool sized for your P95 concurrency and includes cache + faster KV hit assumptions.
- Embeddings cost is modeled separately in the sheet and is ~15% of total cost in the hosted scenario.

Open questions / action items for you:
1) Can you share the historical usage export (token-by-type, daily) for Q4 2025 — that will let us refine the estimate and simulate peaks.
2) Confirm whether the workload needs retained logs longer than 30 days (affects storage & audit pricing).
3) Which SLA tier you expect (standard vs premium with 99.9% and faster backfill windows) — premium changes the support line item.

Next steps: if you share the Q4 export I can update the model and send a line-item invoice-style estimate (PDF) for both Hosted and Dedicated by EOD tomorrow. Mateo (cc'd) will validate the cache/latency assumption once we get the export.

Thanks —
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: Sapphire_cost_model_v1.xlsx (pricing calc, assumptions)
From: Emma Li <emma@getsapphire.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Josh Patel <josh@getsapphire.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 16:30:45 -0800
Subject: Re: Sapphire discovery — initial cost model and next steps

Thanks Camila — really helpful summary. Attaching the Q4 export you asked for (sapphire_usage_q4_2025.csv). A few clarifications after I checked with the engineering team: 

- Token breakdown (rough): 70% generation (median context ~600 tokens), 30% embeddings (batch jobs, slightly spiky at month-end).
- Monthly active users (MAU): ~8k with expected 12% month-on-month growth through H1.
- Budget range: internally we're looking at $12k to $18k per month for inference costs initially — our preference is to stay under $100/1M tokens.
- Questions for Redwood team: will caching reduce effective billable tokens (we hope yes), and how does reserved capacity handle monthly variability? Also need guidance on data residency and retention for PII — will follow up with a security contact if needed.

I'll get you the raw CSV with daily token counts attached. Let me know if you want anything else.

Emma Li
Head of Product | Sapphire Analytics
emma@getsapphire.ai

Attachments: sapphire_usage_q4_2025.csv (daily token-by-type export)
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@getsapphire.ai>, Josh Patel <josh@getsapphire.ai>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 08:10:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Sapphire discovery — initial cost model and next steps

Emma — thanks for the CSV, that was exactly what we needed. I've updated the workbook and exported a short invoice-style PDF (pricing_calc_breakdown.pdf) for easier review — attached. Summary of the updated, conservative scenarios (all numbers monthly):

Scenario A — Hosted (pay-as-you-go):
- Effective monthly: ~$14,400
- Effective $/1M tokens: ~$96
- Notes: assumes live prefix cache hit of ~22%, standard hosted SLAs; elastic handling of spikes (no commit)

Scenario B — Dedicated (12mo commitment + autoscale reserve):
- Effective monthly run-rate: ~$10,500 (after committed discount)
- Effective $/1M tokens: ~$70
- Notes: lower unit economics because of sustained commit and higher cache assumptions; adds a fixed monthly reserved capacity line item + priority support

Assumptions (short):
- Q4 usage patterns applied with 10% growth buffer
- Average generation context: 600 tokens
- Embedding unit costs modeled per 1K vectors at current open-embedding rate
- Network and storage included at standard enterprise rates; longer retention or HSM key usage would add a line item

If you want a tailored PO/invoice for procurement I can produce a draft with exact line items (compute, cache, storage, support) and suggested billing cadence. Also looping Mateo to validate the cache hit assumptions and confirm whether a small quantization change on the model side could further reduce run-rate.

Would you prefer we model a 6-month pilot commit vs 12-month? That changes break-even on Dedicated.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing_calc_breakdown.pdf, Sapphire_cost_model_v1.xlsx

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 09:12:03 -0800
Subject: Re: Sapphire discovery — technical notes on caching & quantization (internal)

Camila / Ben — quick technical note before we send the final invoice: 

- Cache: for the chat-heavy traffic with ~600 token context and 20-25% repeated prefixes, realistic steady-state cache hit of 20-25% is achievable with a warm KV cache. That reduces billable token generation by the same factor (modeled in the spreadsheet).
- Quantization: switching to 4-bit quantized variants for the non-critical summarization workloads saves about 6–9% on GPU utilization for Dedicated and reduces per-inference cost ~8% in our sim. Worth including as an optional checkbox in the SOW.
- Reserved sizing: to hit the Dedicated run-rate in the workbook, we'll size for P95 concurrency (~75) and allow a 20% autoscale buffer for monthly spikes — recommended to start with a 3-month review window and tune after the pilot.

I'll review the updated XLS and flag any places where we should be more conservative. If you want, I can join the next call with Sapphire to run through the line items.

— Mateo
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
